text_original: Collector paraphrase (not verbatim source text): Reviewer measured 5.0 mi/kWh in everyday driving (about 440 miles) and 3.2 mi/kWh at motorway speeds (about 282 miles). Reviewer states the car held 296 kW from 10-40% and still pulled over 80 kW at 90%. Reviewer states the secondary ride is jittery over rutted surfaces and sharp inputs, whereas a BMW i5 M Sport moves with more grace and agility over bumpy roads. Reviewer calls it arguably the nicest cabin in its class and expects drivers coming from the BMW i5 to be impressed by its ambience. Reviewer states some hard plastics feel cheap and the column stalks have some play. Reviewer criticises window controls in the touchscreen, mirror adjustment that is hard to reach quickly and a fog light that needs a physical button. Reviewer reports some wind noise near the driver-side B-pillar, possibly an early-build seal issue. Reviewer states the adaptive regeneration mode is less natural than Mercedes' and wants an intermediate setting. Reviewer rates the 424-litre boot as average, below the BMW i5's 520 litres, though the hatchback opening helps. Reviewer states rear knee room is class-leading. Reviewer states front-seat comfort is class-leading and the driving position feels raised yet planted. Reviewer considers the Ultra with air springs (from GBP 77,260) expensive next to a well-optioned VW ID.7. Reviewer states build quality is good but not universally at BMW level. Original excerpt(s), from tool summaries: «plasticky»
